digest.component_or_area: external integration test / completion tool policy
propositions: The live external integration test test_dense_completion_banks_and_terminates_in_two_of_three_trials deterministically fails 0/3 trials with calls_at_bank=[11,11,11,11,11] after commit e1352535ace changed completion_tool_policy to execute batched evidence calls instead of suppressing them

The test oracle _bounded_bank_gaps measures bounded gaps in executed filesystem-tool calls (pre-dd41 unit) while the enforcement boundary in completion_tool_policy is denominated in evidence RESPONSES (max_evidence_responses=3), decoupling the two units after dd41's intentional per-KIND claims refactor
Batching models execute ~11 reads in <=2 evidence responses post-dd41, never reaching the 3-response fallback boundary, making the executed-call-denominated oracle structurally unsatisfiable

The production behavior (batched governed reads, response-denominated boundary) is intended and proven correct; the test is the defective artifact requiring re-denomination to evidence responses to preserve the original 0707 safety intent

The test repair re-denominates oracle measurement and bounds from executed calls to distinct evidence-response run_steps while preserving the safety invariant of incremental banking with bounded gaps and no zero-bank exhaustion

A new unit regression in test_completion_banking_oracle.py drives the shared response-counting helpers through the real wrap_completion_evidence_policy to prove the batched shape is accepted and the original defect shapes (zero banks, unbounded first bank) are rejected
